successors.note: The Bundesrat voted on 8 December 1870 and the Reichstag on 10 December 1870 to rename the Confederation 'German Empire'; the 1871 constitution took effect on 1 January 1871 and the Empire was founded on 18 January 1871.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1867: Cliopatria's row begins in 1868, but the constitution 'went into effect on 1 July 1867'. The shape is the 1868 one (365,060 km2 against Prussia's 348,607 km2 in the member table, ratio 1.05). The table totals 412,517 km2 for 23 members; Prussia 'had four-fifths of the Confederation's territory and population, more than the other 21 members combined'. Cliopatria draws only the Prussian share; the other members (Saxony, the Mecklenburgs, Oldenburg, Anhalt, Brunswick, the Thuringian duchies and principalities, Lippe, Waldeck, the three Hanse cities and Oberhessen) stay separate rows with their own dossiers to 1870 and are not added here, so that no cell is drawn twice.

keyframe_review.note: 365,060 km2 for 1868-1869 against 348,607 km2 for Prussia in the page's member table (ratio 1.05; the 1866 annexations of Hanover, Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, Frankfurt and Schleswig-Holstein are inside). The page's total for all 23 members is 412,517 km2; the 64,000 km2 difference is the other 22 members, which Cliopatria keeps as separate rows (checked: no cell of the 1868 shape lies in the 1868 shapes of Mecklenburg, Saxony, Anhalt, Hesse, Hamburg, Oldenburg, Bavaria or Brunswick).

The 1870 shape (449,072 km2) is the 1868 shape plus 369 cells (about 85,000 km2) in north-eastern France (Marne, Aisne, Aube, Meuse, Moselle, Vosges, Ardennes, Meurthe-et-Moselle, Oise, Seine-et-Marne, Bas-Rhin, Haut-Rhin and more, bbox 1.7-8.3 E, 47.8-50.4 N) and the Bavarian Palatinate. France was only invaded: 'invaded northeastern France on 4 August'; the war ran 'from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871' and Alsace-Lorraine was ceded only by the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871). The French departments are occupied or contested land, not Confederation territory, and the Palatinate belongs to Bavaria (a separate row to 1870).

correction.text: the 1868 shape unchanged: the Confederation's land is Prussia's territory; the French departments are contested in 1870 (contest events) and the Palatinate is Bavaria's

ledger.note: 1867: the North German Confederation takes effect under Prussian leadership. 'The revised constitution was passed on 16 April 1867 by a vote of 230 to 53' and 'it went into effect on 1 July 1867'; the founding treaty was signed on 18 August 1866 by 'Prussia and fifteen north and central German states'. The lead says it existed 'from July 1867 to December 1870'. 3 Nov 2026 (fx-53 D03): Prussia is a member of the Confederation, not its predecessor. 'Prussia and fifteen north and central German states signed the North German Confederation Treaty' and Prussia 'had four-fifths of the Confederation's territory and population, more than the other 21 members combined' (North German Confederation page). The counterpart kingdom-of-prussia and the predecessors entry were removed, because the compiler takes a found's counterpart and the predecessors' cells outright (and R2 hands a successor every conflict with its predecessor) while kingdom-of-prussia is alive to November 1918 (fx-45 R121); the claim on Prussia's cells is now an ordinary conflict that Prussia wins (R3 constituent once data/hierarchy.csv has the row kingdom-of-prussia -> north-german-confederation 1867-1870, the size rule until then).

region.text: Prussia's whole territory, 348,607 km2, 'four-fifths of the Confederation's territory and population'; Prussia stays alive as a member (constituent) of the Confederation, so this claim is a conflict the member wins

ledger.note: 4 August 1870: German armies invade north-eastern France. 'France invaded German territory on 2 August' (Saarbrucken) and the German coalition 'invaded northeastern France on 4 August', first at Wissembourg. The zone is Cliopatria's 1870 growth inside France; the page names Alsace, Lorraine, Orleans, Amiens, Le Mans and Belfort as places of fighting but no departments.

region.text: north-eastern France as the Germans held or fought over it in 1870

ledger.note: 2 September 1870: Napoleon III surrenders at Sedan. 'By the next day, on 2 September, Napoleon III surrendered and was taken prisoner with 104,000 of his soldiers'; on 4 September 'a provisional government called the Government of National Defence' was proclaimed, so the Empire as an opponent ends here.
September 1870: the war goes on against the Government of National Defence. 'Prussian forces commenced the siege of Paris on 19 September 1870'; the new republic is the french-third-republic dossier.

region.text: north-eastern France and the approaches to Paris

ledger.note: December 1870: the Confederation becomes the German Empire while the war is still on. The war ran 'from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871' (truce of 28 January); the contest with the republic continues in the german-empire ledger, which closes it on the truce. The pairing here ends with the Confederation, not with the fighting.

December 1870: the Confederation is renamed German Empire. On 8 December 1870 the Bundesrat 'voted in favour of changing the Confederation's name to German Empire (Deutsches Reich)'; the amendment 'passed the Reichstag on 10 December 1870'; 'in November 1870' Baden, Bavaria, Wurttemberg and Hesse signed treaties that 'brought them into the Confederation'; 'The 1871 Constitution ... became effective on 1 January 1871' and the Empire was founded on 18 January 1871.

wars.outcome: German victory: the war ran from 19 July 1870 to 28 January 1871; the German states proclaimed their union as the German Empire; France ceded most of Alsace and parts of Lorraine by the Treaty of Frankfurt (10 May 1871).
wars.note: The Confederation is a party until 31 December 1870; the German Empire's ledger carries January 1871 onwards.

certainty.note: Prussia's 1866 annexations were made into provinces with provincial boundaries; the frontier with the southern states along the Main is a state boundary. The French zone of 1870 is a soft, shifting front.

notes: Cliopatria draws the Confederation as Prussia's territory only (checked against the 1868 shapes of eight member states: no overlap). The other members (the page's table lists 23 incl. Prussia, 412,517 km2) are separate rows; the German Empire's ledger adds them at 1871-01. If the compile wants the federation as one territory it should union the member shapes; this dossier does not, to avoid drawing a cell twice. The 1870 shape is Prussia plus 369 cells in north-eastern France and the Bavarian Palatinate: verdict adjust (contested, not owned). Page silent: which French departments were held at which date; the 1871-73 occupation is in the french-third-republic and german-empire dossiers. No Wikipedia page for the Confederation gives an 'Established' infobox field; 1 July 1867 is the text's date. The German Confederation (1815-1866) dissolved before the start; its dossier belongs to another group. REALM OF MEMBER STATES (fx-53 D03, 3 Nov 2026): kingdom-of-prussia is a member (constituent) of the Confederation from 1 July 1867 to December 1870 and lives on to November 1918, so it is no longer listed in identity.predecessors and the 1867 found no longer names it as counterpart; Prussia keeps its own land and the Confederation holds only cells that no member holds (the other members, Saxony, the Mecklenburgs, Oldenburg and the rest, already have constituent rows in data/hierarchy.csv; the row for kingdom-of-prussia, 1867-1870, is for the orchestrator). Page (North German Confederation, opened 3 Nov 2026): 'Prussia and fifteen north and central German states signed the North German Confederation Treaty'; 'It had four-fifths of the Confederation's territory and population, more than the other 21 members combined'; the Confederation existed 'from July 1867 to December 1870'; 'it went into effect on 1 July 1867'; the Bundesrat 'voted in favour of changing the Confederation's name to "German Empire"'. The Confederation's keyframes stay Prussia's territory (Cliopatria's shape), now tinted as the member's land.
